title: The road less travelled part 3
scripture_text: ’’After this, Jesus travelled about from one town and village to another, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with him, and also some women who had been cured of evil spirits and diseases: Mary (called Magdalene from whom seven demons had come out; Joanna the wife of Chuza, the manager of Herod’s household; Susanna; and many others. These women were helping to support them out of their own means.’’
devotional:
To follow Jesus will help us to become as human as Him.

I have often thought that the problem with our humanity is that we are not human enough. As we are going to see the road of discipleship is one of the things God uses to make us more human. Our sin dehumanises us, and Jesus wants to reverse and eventually remove the dehumanising effects that sin has had on us.

Luke tells us something that would be very easy to miss it’s impact. ‘and many others were contributing from their own resources to support Jesus and his disciples.’ Let these two words sink into your heart. ‘Support Jesus,’ I think most of us would feel slightly uncomfortable with the idea of supporting Jesus! The word Luke uses for support is diakoneo were our word deacon comes from.

Mark Hepner states that ‘A survey of the uses of diakoneo in the NT indicates a basic meaning of “giving someone what is necessary to sustain their physical life.” sermonindex.net accessed 16/03/2025

Consequently the word is frequently used in the gospels to mean “set food before someone” or “wait on someone.” This is very important because Jesus chose to become dependent on others. Why? Because he wanted to teach us how to be human, he wanted to show the glorious essence of our humanity. Let me explain. Jesus had a God-given ability to do the miraculous, he was able to feed over 5000 people with 5 small loafs and 2 fish. But he never used his divine power to meet his own needs, he never turned stone into bread.

It was as if Jesus as a perfect man valued the relationships of dependence more than independence. He would rather receive from those who loved him, than use his power to meet his own needs. The road of discipleship teaches us that to be as human as Jesus, is to receive from others. Sometimes people can become so dehumanised by their pride they are unable to receive from others. You often hear people say something like ‘I am not a charity case.’ you know what? we are all charity cases. We all need the support, love and grace of others. As these women followed Jesus, they got to know someone who was vulnerable enough to receive. Jesus’ vulnerability to receive allowed him to be really known by others. He was unafraid of reality or intimacy.

Think how it must have affected these women as they supported Jesus. I don’t believe for one moment that they supported Jesus with some kind of hidden agenda, or that they gave so they would feel good about themselves. However, when Jesus received from them, it must have filled their hearts with great joy and gave them a deep sense of acceptance.
prayer: Father thank you for every opportunity to minister onto Jesus.

The road less travelled part 3

Study Text: Luke 8:1-3
’’After this, Jesus travelled about from one town and village to another, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with him, and also some women who had been cured of evil spirits and diseases: Mary (called Magdalene from whom seven demons had come out; Joanna the wife of Chuza, the manager of Herod’s household; Susanna; and many others.
